Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Observability alert: gen-v2 p99 tail spike during onboarding burst

Team —

Monitoring picked up a sustained p99 increase for model gen-v2 starting ~08:12 PDT coincident with the Nimbus Health onboarding ramp. Summary: p50 stable, p95 +12% , p99 jumped from 420ms baseline to ~1.8s for a sustained 22 minutes, with sporadic 3.1s outliers. Error rates are nominal (<=0.1%).

Initial telemetry:
- Host-level: GPU utilization rose from 64% to 93% on worker pool a-nv24x:85
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% during prefix-heavy requests
- Request mix: longer sequences (avg tokens/request +40%) from onboarding flows

Immediate asks: can Eng confirm if a recent rollout to gen-v2 configuration (kernel selector tweak) landed in the US pool in the 07:45–08:00 window? Also, we should prepare an outbound customer note and a short mitigation plan for Nimbus.

Attaching quick snapshot: p99_spike_summary.pdf (metrics + span traces).

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
SRE, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 18, 2026 at 08:23 Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monitoring picked up a sustained p99 increase for model gen-v2 starting ~08:12 PDT ...

Quick update from Eng triage:
- Rollout check: there was a kernel-selection heuristic change deployed to the canary pool at 07:40 and promoted to us-west-1 at 07:53. I believe a variant of that heuristic caused less favorable kernel selection for long-sequence requests, which explains the p99 jump under prefix-heavy onboarding traffic.
- Root cause hypothesis: heuristic favors smaller kernels for throughput optimization; for long sequences it increases CPU->GPU stalls and causes KV-cache pressure.

Short-term mitigations we can enact in the next 20–35 minutes:
1) Immediate rollback of the kernel-selection tweak in the us-west replica set (estimated 15 min to roll).
2) Apply a per-customer routing rule to send Nimbus traffic to a stable gen-v2 variant (gen-v2-stable) — ~10 min to flip and test.
3) Increase KV cache allocation on affected hosts (risk: memory pressure) — ~25–40 min.

Suggested order: flip routing for Nimbus first (fast, low-risk), then rollback the heuristic if we see residual tail. I'll open RED-4523 and attach a runbook for the rollback path.

Attachments: mitigation-runbook-v1.md (runbook + rollback steps).

— Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
